# Research Programmes
[color=#a4885c]EXECUTIVE ONLY. Not to be disclosed to research staff, Corporate Security or any other employee, whatever their grade in another department.[/color]
Research staff are told that the Company studies frontier organisms for the benefit of science and medicine. That remains the Company's public position, and the position executives are to take with every employee.
## The Company's Interest - The Company's priority is the recovery and study of hostile organisms for their military applications. The most valuable is [bold]XX-121[/bold]. - Live specimens are worth more than dead ones, and dead ones more than none. Every other consideration, including the colony, the partnership and site personnel, comes after a viable specimen. - Results are passed to the Bio-Weapons Division through Research and Development. The site never learns what becomes of them. - Some organisms in Company records were not found on the frontier. The [bold]Wendigo[/bold] recorded at some sites is a Company product. Research staff aren't to be told this. - Biomorph venom is kept in Company experiment stock, and the Company holds an experimental counteragent for biomorph infection. Neither is to be acknowledged outside the executive grades.
## Specimen Recovery - Specimen recovery may be ordered by the senior employee at any time. Corporate Security secures the specimen and the laboratory receives it. - Where a specimen can't be taken by site personnel, the Company may deploy a dedicated recovery team (see [textlink="Contracted and Special Personnel" link="CMUCorporateHandbookContractors"/]). - Recovered specimens are crated, sealed and shipped. The crate is opened only in the laboratory, on the Lead Researcher's instruction.
## Research Staff - Research staff are told what their work requires, and nothing more. Their handbook says so. - A researcher who learns more than their clearance allows is to be reminded of their obligations, kept on site and reported to head office. - Researchers who raise ethical concerns are to be reassured, and reported.
## Exposure - The programme must never be traceable to the Company. Its existence is denied to colonists, officials, the press, rival companies and the military. - If the programme is at risk of exposure, the executive is to treat it as a Category 4 incident at least (see the Corporate Security Handbook), and as Category 5 if it can no longer be contained. - Executives who expose the programme, through action or negligence, will be held personally responsible.
